compiled:
📰 General

Winter Storm Threatens Atlanta with Freezing Rain and Significant Ice Accumulation •

A major winter storm is currently impacting Atlanta, Georgia, with freezing rain and ice expected from Saturday evening through Monday morning. The National Weather Service forecasts widespread freezing rain, potentially leading to a quarter of the metro area experiencing significant ice accumulation. Travel disruptions are anticipated across the region due to hazardous road conditions. Authorities are urging residents to prepare for potential power outages and to monitor ongoing updates from the National Weather Service.

🌍 World

Russian Strikes Against Ukraine Claim One Life, Injure Dozens Before Talks Begin •

Russian forces launched attacks across Ukraine overnight, resulting in the death of one individual and the injury of 31 people. The attacks targeted multiple locations, including the capital city of Kyiv. Negotiations between Ukraine, Russia, and the United States are currently underway in the United Arab Emirates, aiming to establish a framework for a ceasefire. These discussions follow a similar meeting yesterday and are focused on addressing key security concerns. The situation remains volatile as the talks progress.

🦅 US

Google’s Gmail Opt-In: Users Can Now Disable AI Training Data Access •

Google’s Gmail service includes an automatic opt-in that allows the company to use user email data for artificial intelligence training. This setting, recently highlighted by tech publications, grants Google access to conversations and attachments within Gmail accounts. Users can proactively disable this feature within their Google account settings to prevent data from being utilized for AI development. The change allows users to maintain greater control over their personal information within the popular email service.

💰 Business

Gore-Tex Pioneer Gore Wear Announces Permanent Closure After 51 Years •

Gore Wear, the 51-year-old athletic wear brand known for its Gore-Tex technology, is closing its doors permanently. The company cited evolving consumer preferences and market dynamics as key factors in its decision. Gore Wear has historically catered to athletes who train and compete in challenging weather conditions, prioritizing performance over traditional weather forecasts. Despite its innovative products and strong brand recognition, the company determined it could no longer sustain operations in the current market landscape. This closure marks the end of an era for the brand’s commitment to outdoor athletic apparel.

💻 Technology

Kill Team: Shadowhunt Launches with Devastating Aerial Assault – Pre-Orders Now Live •

The Kill Team: Shadowhunt, a new addition to the Warhammer 40,000 universe, has launched with pre-orders available. The initial release focuses on Space Marines utilizing jump packs and flensing blades. These units are designed to engage opponents from aerial positions, creating a dynamic and potentially dangerous combat scenario. The campaign emphasizes a terrifying tactic of descending attackers, highlighting a key element of the Kill Team’s strategy. The release aims to deliver a visceral and impactful experience for players.

🎭 Entertainment

Kirsten Dunst Defends Jesse Plemons’ “Bugonia” Oscar Snub with a Memorable Response •

Following the Academy Award nominations, actress Kirsten Dunst addressed the perceived oversight regarding her husband, Jesse Plemons’ performance in “Bugonia.” She responded by sharing a meme from a colleague involved in the film. The meme appears to be a lighthearted reaction to the film’s exclusion from major categories. Dunst’s action suggests a supportive stance towards Plemons’ work and the film’s reception.

🏅 Sports

Mavericks-Lakers Game Scheduled Despite Winter Storm Threat in Dallas •

The Dallas Mavericks will proceed with their upcoming game against the Los Angeles Lakers this Saturday. The team confirmed the scheduled contest will take place as planned at 7:30 p.m. Central Time. The decision was made following a winter storm impacting North Texas, which caused icy conditions and travel disruptions. Officials determined the arena and surrounding areas were deemed safe for operation.

🔬 Science

Renowned Chemist Edith Flanigen, Pioneer of Synthetic Materials, Passes at 96 •

Edith Flanigen, a highly respected chemist, died at the age of 96. She achieved prominence at Union Carbide through her groundbreaking research into synthetic emeralds and complex materials. Flanigen’s work significantly contributed to advancements in refining crude oil into gasoline and developing methods for water purification. Her research also played a key role in enhancing the production of various consumer products.

🩺 Health

Adult Contagious with Measles Identified at Ridgefield High School •

Clark County Public Health is investigating a confirmed case of measles in an adult student. The individual was recently traveling from an area with an ongoing measles outbreak and was present at Ridgefield High School on January 1st. Health officials are working to identify potential contacts and prevent further spread. The school is taking precautionary measures, including increased cleaning and monitoring.
